Summary  
Data source overview: The paper “Pre-trained Transformers Improve Out-of-Distribution Robustness” systematically compares bag-of-words, LSTM and several Transformer models on seven NLP tasks under natural distribution shifts. It shows that (1) accuracy drops for traditional models can exceed 35 %, while RoBERTa sometimes improves; (2) pre-trained Transformers detect OOD inputs substantially better (far lower FAR95); (3) robustness gains come from data diversity rather than model size; (4) knowledge-distillation hurts robustness; (5) simple confidence-thresholding already yields usable OOD detectors, but head-room remains. The authors release a benchmark that induces realistic shifts in genre, topic and vocabulary.  

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[86]  
Inference strategy justification: All risk→intervention causal chains appear explicitly or are straightforward one-step inferences (marked with confidence 2) from statements such as “pretrained on diverse data aids robustness”.  
Extraction completeness: 26 nodes (≈15/5 000 w) cover every distinct claim, mechanism, finding and intervention that the paper uses in its core reasoning. All nodes are inter-connected; no satellites.  
Key limitations: 1) The paper’s discussion of self-supervised objectives is brief, so edges relating to them are medium confidence. 2) Compression-robustness trade-off is only illustrated with DistilBERT; wider evidence is missing. 3) Benchmarks are treated as implementation mechanisms although they are partly artefacts; this is necessary to keep fabric connected.  

How the instruction set could be improved:  
• Provide an explicit edge type such as “explained_by” for links that clarify but do not mitigate a problem.  
• Allow grouping closely related validation findings to reduce repetition (e.g. combine multiple accuracy metrics into one node).  
• Clarify whether “design rationale” may connect directly to a risk when no problem-analysis node is available.
